routes.label: Find the largest selection with too few pairs

question: A drawer in a darkened room contains \(100\) red socks, \(80\) green socks, \(60\) blue socks and \(40\) black socks. A youngster selects socks one at a time from the drawer but is unable to see the color of the socks drawn. What is the smallest number of socks that must be selected to guarantee that the selection contains at least \(10\) pairs? (A pair of socks is two socks of the same color. No sock may be counted in more than one pair.)
solution:
To find when ten pairs are guaranteed, first find how many socks could be selected while still having at most nine pairs.

Within each color, form disjoint pairs until no more can be made. At most one sock of each color remains unpaired, since two remaining socks of that color would form another pair. Thus a selection with at most nine pairs contains at most
\[
2\cdot9+4=22
\]
socks. Consequently, every selection of 23 socks contains at least ten pairs.

To show that 22 socks are insufficient, select 19 red socks and one sock of each other color. These quantities are available in the drawer, and the selection contains exactly nine red pairs and no pairs of another color. Therefore the smallest guaranteed number is \(23\), choice B.

answerCheck.reason: With at most nine pairs there can be at most 18 paired socks plus one unpaired sock of each of four colors, totaling 22. A draw of 19 red and one of each other color attains 22 with only nine pairs, so 23 is necessary and sufficient.
